item.title: Stock market: US Supreme Court rejects Trump tariffs; Gift Nifty jumps 320 points; analysts views
item.description: “The development has buoyed global markets, with GIFT Nifty rising over 1%, indicating the possibility of a gap-up opening for the Nifty at the start of the week, barring any fresh adverse global triggers," Hariprasad said.

item.title: GTRI urges India to reassess US trade deal after Supreme Court's Trump tariff ruling
item.description: India and the US are in advanced negotiations over an interim trade deal, with Indian officials due to travel to Washington to finalise the agreement’s text. The timing of the Supreme Court’s ruling, just weeks after both nations issued a joint statement outlining the contours of the deal, adds fresh complexities to the negotiations.

item.title: 'No proposal to create BRICS currency': Lula da Silva's pushback against de-dollarisation claims
item.description: He called the conversation around de-dollarisation "misunderstood".

item.title: Delhi on high alert after Intel warns of LeT threat to Red Fort, Chandni Chowk area: Report
item.description: According to intelligence sources, Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) is reportedly orchestrating plans to target these sites, as part of a wider strategy.

item.title: Indus by Sarvam: A first look at India’s homegrown AI chat app built for local languages
item.description: Indus functions as the public interface for Sarvam’s newly introduced 105-billion-parameter model. Its knowledge cuts off at June 2025.

item.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump tariffs: Samir Arora says, ‘understanding is more important than just open markets’
item.description: “We should stop asking for stock markets to be open for every economic announcement so that traders can hedge their risks,” Arora wrote on Saturday.

item.title: Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs struck down: India's tariff rate down to 10%, how the revised duty would work and more
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled with a 6-3 majority that the Trump administration exceeded its legal authority by using the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to impose broad-based tariffs without congressional approval.
